payload.excerpt: A sand ceremony script your celebrant can read word for word, with original sample wording in several tones, a fill-in template, what to set on the table and the questions to ask before you pour sand on a beach.
key_takeaways: Every script works in three parts: the celebrant introduces the ritual, you pour, and the celebrant closes the moment.
A sand ceremony is symbolic, so it sits beside the legal words of your ceremony and never takes their place.
The pour fits neatly after the vows and rings and before the pronouncement, and your celebrant sets the final order.
On a beach or abroad, ask the venue or local council about wind, sealing the vessel and whether sand may be taken from the shore.

faq.q: What do you say at a sand ceremony?
faq.a: Your celebrant introduces the ritual, invites you to pour, then closes the moment with a line or two. The couple need say nothing at all. The scripts above give each part word for word.

faq.q: Do you do the sand ceremony before or after the vows?
faq.a: The pour fits neatly after the vows and rings, just before the pronouncement, or straight after the welcome. Agree the order with your celebrant, and keep the pour clear of the legal lines.

A sand ceremony is a symbolic ritual you choose, and it sits as comfortably in a civil ceremony as in a religious one. If a minister of religion is marrying you, ask where a sand moment can sit within their rite.

faq.q: What do you need for a sand ceremony?
faq.a: One clear keepsake vessel, a small carafe for each person pouring, sand in contrasting colours, a small table, a funnel and a lid to seal the vessel afterwards.

faq.q: How do you include children in a sand ceremony?
faq.a: Give each child their own colour and a carafe small enough to hold in one hand. Let them pour first, then pour your colours over the top, and have the celebrant speak to them by name.

faq.q: How long does a sand ceremony take?
faq.a: The classic script above takes a couple of minutes with the pour. A family pour with several carafes runs a little longer. For the full running time of your day, see [how long a wedding ceremony runs](/expert-advice/how-long-is-a-wedding-ceremony).
